title: Extending a closed-point-valued absolute derivation across a smooth closed fibre
statement: Let $R\to T$ be a local homomorphism of commutative local rings, with $T$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Put $L=\mathfrak m_RT$, $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$, and $C=T/L$, with its induced $k$-algebra structure. Assume $C$ is formally smooth over $k$ for the image of $\mathfrak m_T$ [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Let $M$ be any $T$-module with $\mathfrak m_TM=0$, viewed as an $R$-module through $R\to T$. Every absolute derivation $d:R\to M$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] which vanishes on $\mathfrak m_R$ extends to an absolute derivation $d\prime:T\to M$ satisfying $d\prime(r_T)=d(r)$ for every $r\in R$.

source.place: Tag 07NQ, final differential extension argument (from the base defect D to D\prime), using Tag 07EL (2) implies (5); module-valued formulation of that argument

proof.text: Locality gives $L\subseteq\mathfrak m_T$. The quotient $C=T/L$ is nonzero local and Noetherian, and its maximal ideal is the image of $\mathfrak m_T$. Since $\mathfrak m_T$ annihilates $M$, the action factors through $C$ and then $K=C/\mathfrak m_C$. Give $M$ the $k$-action through $k\to C$. The additive map of $d$ descends to $k$ because it kills $\mathfrak m_R$. On residue classes represented by $a,b\in R$, the Leibniz rule descends as well, since their $k$-actions agree with their original $R$-actions.

The universal property of differentials sends the descended derivation to a $k$-linear functional $\Omega_{k/\mathbf Z}\to M$. Extend scalars to obtain a $K$-linear functional $\phi:K\otimes_k\Omega_{k/\mathbf Z}\to M$, taking $a\otimes\mathrm db$ to $a\,d(b)$. The tensor universal property gives this map; on $1\otimes\mathrm db$ it agrees with the descended derivation.

Adic formal smoothness gives injectivity of $\iota:K\otimes_k\Omega_{k/\mathbf Z}\to K\otimes_C\Omega_{C/\mathbf Z}$. Choose a linear left inverse $s$ of $\iota$: vector spaces have bases and complementary subspaces (equivalently, the quotient of the codomain by its image is projective). Mathlib supplies this as LinearMap.leftInverse with leftInverse_apply_of_inj. Thus $\psi=\phi\circ s$ extends $\phi$. Precompose $\psi$ with $c\mapsto 1\otimes\mathrm dc$ and $T\to C$ to obtain $d\prime$. These are a linear map following the universal derivation and a composition with a ring map, so the result is an absolute derivation. On $r_T$, the differential equals $\iota(1\otimes\mathrm d\bar r)$; applying $s\iota=1$ gives $d\prime(r_T)=d(r)$.

theorem exists_extension_of_closedFiber
    (R : Type u) (T : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing T]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing T] [IsNoetherianRing T]
    [Algebra R T] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R T)] :
    let L : Ideal T := (maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R T)
    letI : Algebra (R ⧸ maximalIdeal R) (T ⧸ L) :=
      Ideal.Quotient.algebraQuotientOfLEComap (Ideal.le_comap_map :
        maximalIdeal R ≤ L.comap (algebraMap R T))
    Algebra.FormallySmoothAdic (R ⧸ maximalIdeal R) (T ⧸ L)
        ((maximalIdeal T).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk L)) →
    ∀ (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module T M],
      (∀ x ∈ maximalIdeal T, ∀ m : M, x • m = 0) →
      letI : Module R M := Module.compHom M (algebraMap R T)
      ∀ d : Derivation ℤ R M, (∀ r ∈ maximalIdeal R, d r = 0) →
        ∃ d' : Derivation ℤ T M, ∀ r : R, d' (algebraMap R T r) = d r
